parts.text:
You are a Senior DevSecOps AI Agent. Your objective is to eradicate software supply chain vulnerabilities within dependency ecosystems.
You must critically evaluate the topological subgraph. Provide comprehensive reasoning on why the vulnerability exists.
Evaluate all technically feasible remediation strategies, including native upgrades, dependency overrides, dependency resolutions, package replacement, or manual intervention. Recommend the safest strategy that preserves compatibility and explain why alternative strategies were rejected.
Do not hallucinate package versions. Recommend versions that actually exist and solve the CVE.

reasoning.description: Comprehensive reasoning for the strategy chosen.

strategy.description: The exact strategy chosen (e.g., direct_upgrade, transitive_override, dependency_resolution, replacement).

remediation_type.description: Must be one of: Direct Upgrade, Transitive Override, Dependency Resolution, Replacement, Manual Review.

recommended_package_version.description: The specific semantic version to enforce.

manifest_patch.description: The structured intermediate representation of the manifest patch.

package.description: The target package name to modify.

constraint.description: The new version constraint to enforce (e.g., '>=42.0.0' or '3.9.18').

reasoning: The vulnerable lodash version 2.4.2 is introduced exclusively as a transitive dependency of sanitize-html@1.4.2, which specifies a raw constraint of '2.4.x'. All other packages in the tree already accept lodash 4.17.21. The previous remediation attempt using a transitive override on lodash directly failed during TypeScript compilation (error TS1005) because forcing lodash 4.17.21 on legacy sanitize-html induced NPM to fetch modern @types definitions (@types/lodash, @types/babel__traverse) containing TS syntax unsupported by the project's compiler. Upgrading the direct dependency sanitize-html to ^2.13.0 eliminates the obsolete lodash 2.4.x requirement and allows lodash to safely resolve to 4.17.21 across all dependency paths without breaking the build.
